Subject: Egress origin evidence + signed attestation request for private endpoint

Hi Jordan / EternaHealth Audit team,

Thanks for the onboarding call earlier. As part of the private endpoint review for the VPC deployment, Security needs a compact evidence package showing outbound origination for traffic to Redwood control plane (private endpoint). Specifically, we need: 

- Packet capture sample(s) showing TLS handshakes / SNI for 30 minutes of representative traffic from your gateway to our endpoints (pcap stub is fine).
- IP address ranges and ASN for the egress IPs observed during the capture.
- mTLS / client-certificate validation evidence if you’re fronting traffic through a proxy.
- A short signed attestation (one page) from your network/security lead confirming the above and the retention policy for the captures (30 days minimum).
- Any NAT or proxy translation mapping (original private IPs -> egress nat IPs) for the time window.

Attachments: we’ll accept: a pcap subset, a CSV tally of SNI/FQDN hits, and a signed attestation PDF/Doc. I attached a signed-attestation-template.docx to speed the process. If you prefer to send a link to an artifact bundle (Drive/S3) that’s fine.

Timeline: given the compliance window, can you aim to share an initial bundle by EOD Friday (2026-12-11)? If you can’t meet that, please propose another date.

Operational notes: Ben and Laura are copied to take any technical questions on the capture format and acceptable fields. If you need us to pre-provision a temporary monitoring endpoint or a small sampling script we can provide one.

Thanks —

--
Camila Reyes

2) Which time window should we sample? We can do a rolling 30-minute sample during peak traffic or an off-peak window.
3) For the attestation: do you need a notarized/DocuSign-signed version or a signed PDF from our security manager?

We anticipate delivering the initial bundle by 2026-12-10 COB if we do a targeted 30-minute peak sample. I’ve opened a secure share at: https://files.eternahc.com/secure/egress/REDACTED (link expires in 7 days). We’ll upload a pcap subset (pcap.gz), sni-tally.csv, and a signed PDF.

Jordan — thanks for the quick turnaround and the secure share link. A few specifics from the Redwood security checklist to make sure the bundle is consumable by our audit team: 

- PCAP: please include at least TCP/TLS headers and the Server Name Indication (SNI) fields. If you cannot export full payload, include a per-packet JSON summary that has timestamp, src_ip, src_port, dest_ip, dest_port, tls_client_hello_sni, tls_version, and cipher suite.
- SNI tally: CSV with columns: timestamp_window_start, timestamp_window_end, observed_fqdn, hit_count, sample_percent.
- NAT mapping: a short mapping table (CSV or plain text) that maps internal source IPs -> public egress IP with timestamp ranges.
- Attestation: The attestation should state that the captures were taken from the production egress path to Redwood, the capture retention period (>=30 days), and contact info for the engineer who performed the capture. A DocuSign is ideal but a signed PDF from your security manager is acceptable.

Additionally, because some customers use a transparent gateway which can rewrite SNI (SNI-less TLS passthrough), if you see any TLS sessions without SNI please flag them and include server certificate CN/SANs in the packet summary so we can match them to the control plane.

If helpful I’ve attached a small packet-json exporter script (attachment: pcap-to-json-snippet.txt) we use internally. Happy to run it on a small sample if you prefer we host a collector; that would avoid shipping pcap binaries.

Ben Carter
Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
